simple.meaning: מָסַךְ (mâçak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to mix , especially wine (with spices).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, beginning at Psalms 102:10. Its contexts include Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָסַךְ (H4537).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָסַךְ (mâçak) / H4537 is traced through Psalms 102:10, Proverbs 9:2, Proverbs 9:5, Isaiah 5:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4537. masak מָסַךְ verb mix, produce by mixing (compare perhaps מֶזֶג מזג, Ba ES 33, 51 ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular ׳מ Isa 19:14 ; מָֽסְכָה Prov 9:2 ; מָסָ֑כְתִּי 9:5 ; Psa 102:10 ; Infinitive construct מְסֹךְ Isa 5:22 ; — 1 pour , only figurative, עִוְעִים רוּחַ ׳מ בְּקִרְבָּהּ Isa 19:14 (subject ׳מ ); mix , with accusative שֵׁכָר 5:22 ; i.e. make a choice drink by mixing with spices, etc. (mixing with water came later, compare 2Macc 15:39) Löw p. 419 Frä 162f, 171 f. Now Archaeology 1, 120 Benz Archaeology 95 ; object יַיִן figurative, subject wisdom Prov 9:2 , 5 ; מָסָ֑כְתִּי בִּבְכִי שִׁקֻּוַי Psa 102:10 my drink with weeping have I mixed (see Assyrian [ akâl ] ul âkul, bikîtum kurmati, mê ul aštî, dîmtu maštîtî Zim BP 34 ).

occurrences.englishText: because of your indignation and your wrath;
Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine,
Yahweh has mixed a spirit of perverseness in the middle of her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
